rules: Purchase intent requires evidence of people buying or planning to buy (sales figures or estimates, sell-outs, oversubscribed paid offerings, spending/gift-intent surveys, retailer or manufacturer reports of demand). Listings that exist, brand collections, books for sale and gift guides show supply, not demand.
Articles that restate one underlying dataset (a Pinterest report, a PwC survey, a Barna study, one box-office number) count as one signal.
A criterion scored from assumption rather than evidence is marked not assessed, so it lowers confidence and counts as zero instead of carrying a guessed value.
